newsitem.title: USA: Florida Gov calls for tax increases.
newsitem.headline: Florida Gov calls for tax increases.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles Tuesday urged state lawmakers to expand the gross receipts tax to raise an additional $1.3 billion for school construction over the next five years.

Speaking to a joint session of the state legislature on the opening day of the 1997 session, Chiles also urged Republican leaders in both chambers to raise the state's cigarette tax by 10 cents to fund smoking prevention programs for youth.

Both proposals cames as Chiles, an ardent anti-smoker who has filed a $1.4 billion suit against the industry to recoup Medicaid costs for treating smoking related illnesses, focused on children's issues in his annual state-of-the-state address.

Chiles said the state spent hundreds of millions of dollars over the past few years to build prisons, and must show the same resolve in dealing with children's issues including welfare reform, subsidized day care and adequate classroom space.
"I challenge you, if we can make room for criminals, we can make room for kids," Chiles said.

State Republican leaders applauded Chiles' emphasis on early intervention and children's programming. But they said any talk of a tax increase would fall on deaf ears until Republican lawmakers, who hold a majority in both chambers for the first time in 122 years, are satisfied that state programs are operating efficiently.
"There is going to be a great reluctance on the part of Republicans, in my opinion, to raise taxes," said Tom Slade Chairman of the Republican Party of Florida.

Though dealing mostly in generalities, Chiles specifically called for an expansion of the state's gross receipts tax, a 2.5 percent charge levied against electrical utilities and some telecommunications companies.

Under Chiles' plan, the tax would be extended to cable television providers, water utilities and solid waste disposal companies. The tax would be phased in over the next five years. The gross receipts tax is used to back Florida Board of Education bonds for school construction.
The Democratic governor also called on lawmakers to pass a 10-cent-a pack increase in the state cigarette tax, a hike that would raise an estimated $100 million a year.
